candidates.title: SweepDirection is effectively one-valued in production: Ascending is constructed only inside opening_tree.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module; every production caller passes Descending

evidence.command: git grep -n 'SweepDirection' a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60 -- crates/ | grep -vE 'lib.rs|tree/mod.rs|context.rs:60'; echo '--- cfg(test) boundary in opening_tree.rs ---'; git show a136840d4f2ea137f685f0af6dac04254b983b60:crates/cobre-stochastic/src/tree/opening_tree.rs | grep -nE '#\[cfg\(test\)\]'
evidence.output: opening_tree.rs:14:pub enum SweepDirection {  ...  :123: direction: SweepDirection,  :168: SweepDirection::Ascending => ka.total_cmp(&kb),  :169: SweepDirection::Descending => kb.total_cmp(&ka),  :649/:673/:688/:693/:696/:707/:720 set_solve_order(..., SweepDirection::Descending)  :662 set_solve_order(&keys, SweepDirection::Ascending)  :676 set_solve_order(&keys, SweepDirection::Ascending). cobre-sddp/src/setup/mod.rs:469 set_solve_order(&solve_order_keys, SweepDirection::Descending). cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs:1574/:1870 ... SweepDirection::Descending. --- cfg(test) boundary: opening_tree.rs:438:#[cfg(test)]
evidence.reading: SweepDirection has two variants but only Descending is ever selected outside tests. The two Ascending constructions (opening_tree.rs:662,676) sit above the sole #[cfg(test)] boundary at line 438, so they are unit-test-only. The single production caller in cobre-sddp/src/setup/mod.rs:469 passes Descending, and the only other production reference (cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs) is also test code passing Descending. The Ascending arm (opening_tree.rs:168) and the direction: SweepDirection parameter on set_solve_order (line 120/123) therefore exist only to be exercised by dedicated unit tests (solve_order_ascending_first_is_smallest_key at :659), never reached by any production path. The doc comment ('Purely an ordering policy, with no algorithm-specific meaning', :10-12) is a genericity/L1-purity rationale explaining why the enum carries no engine noun; it is not a reservation of the second variant for a planned feature, and there is no reserved-seam or #[allow] note sanctioning an unwired Ascending path.
evidence.extraChecks: Enum census re-run at baseline: git grep -nE '^\s*(pub )?enum ' a136840d..:crates/cobre-stochastic/src returns exactly 8 pub enum (StochasticError, ComponentProvenance, ClosureRejection, HistoryClass, ParWarning, ClassSampler, SweepDirection, ReductionReason); none is literally one-valued. SweepDirection is the effectively-one-valued case the census target points to.

candidates.fixShape: Collapse the speculative generality: since every production caller sorts largest-key-first, drop the SweepDirection enum and the direction parameter on set_solve_order, making the primitive sort descending unconditionally, and remove the now-dead SweepDirection::Descending argument from the one production caller (cobre-sddp/src/setup/mod.rs:469) plus its test mirrors (cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs). The Ascending-only unit tests then either delete or fold into a private test helper that exercises the comparator directly, so no production surface exists solely to be tested. If instead the ascending ordering is a deliberately reserved seam for a planned selection policy, keep it but add an owner-signed reservation note (the CLAUDE.md 'unwired config is reserved, not dead' pattern) at the enum so the unwired variant reads as reserved rather than as silent speculative generality. Either way keep the fix inside cobre-stochastic (the enum/parameter definition); the caller edit is the named, bounded blast radius. No engine noun and no new abstraction is introduced — this removes generality rather than adding it.
